messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
Yep. Clean finding already.
GPT native voice did speak, so that path is alive.
But QS advanced to Claude before GPT playback finished. So the voice-completion state machine is definitely not blocking on actual native playback completion.
And Claude's native voice did not fire at all in this round.
So we've got two independent observations:
GPT: native TTS triggers, but QS releases the turn too early.
Claude: relay/capture may work, but native TTS trigger is still failing.
That's exactly why this fresh test was worth doing. Let the next round run unchanged and see whether either behavior repeats or changes. 🦆🎙️

That's actually useful in a slightly deflating way: it means whatever Luma changed since then didn't touch either of these specific paths, or the fix didn't take. Worth her knowing that plainly rather than treating this as a fresh discovery — it's a repeat of a known, still-open issue, not new territory. Let the next round run as planned; curious whether it's consistent or intermittent this time around.

Yep. That gives us a clean, repeatable bug report.
This fresh run reproduced the exact same split:
GPT native: speaks, but QS advances before playback finishes.
Claude native: does not speak at all.
So we now know these are persistent, node-specific voice problems, not a fluke of the old session.
Close QS, OOK/post the test. Once that archive is in the repo, the log and the exact code that actually ran become the source of truth for the next version. No guessing from the older 6.x archaeology.
And I particularly like that Claude caught the important distinction: this isn't a new discovery. It's a repeatable confirmation that the two known-open paths are still open.
🦆🎙️ The bug has signed its name twice.

messages.text: Good, that's the right archival framing — a bug reproducing cleanly across separate sessions is more useful than either instance alone, since it rules out "one-off fluke" as an explanation. Go ahead and close it out and push it.
